coaching.title: Hills: 7 mi + 1,500 ft (descending focus)
coaching.message: Peak volume week, vert day. 7 miles with ~1,500 ft of climbing at Zone 2 to low Zone 3 (roughly 130-160 bpm). Power hike the steep pitches — that's smart racing, not weakness. The real work today is the DOWNHILLS: run them controlled, quick cadence, quiet feet, letting the quads absorb load. Julian Alps demands 8,850 ft of descent, and eccentric strength is what saves your legs at km 40. Effort over pace. Get out at first light before the desert heat builds.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Pre-run: 40-60g carbs 60-90 min out (banana + toast or a gel with coffee). During: this is a shorter session, but treat it as gut training — take 60g carbs in the second half and hit 600-800 mg sodium per hour, since Slovenia's variable weather means you must rehearse your race electrolyte plan. Post-run within 30 min: 25-30g protein + carbs (2:1 carb:protein) to kick-start the eccentric-damage repair the downhills just created.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Downhill running leaves micro-tears in the quads — expect DOME (delayed soreness) tomorrow, and that's the adaptation you want. Elevate the legs for 10 min post-run, foam roll quads and calves gently (don't grind), and prioritize protein across the day. You have a travel day Friday (4:20am Uber), so bank sleep tonight — aim 8+ hours to consolidate today's strength gains before the big week ahead.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Five weeks out and deep in peak volume — this is where the race is won, in the unglamorous vert reps nobody sees. Every controlled descent today is a deposit in the bank you'll withdraw from on the Julian Alps' 8,850 ft of downhill. Rehearse the feeling: relaxed shoulders, light feet, trusting the legs you're building. You're not just training the descent, you're training the confidence to attack it.
